key_insight: Training with Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) introduces a gradient inductive bias that steers models toward coherent internal belief states; combining MTP with latent semantic enhancement yields more structured, semantically meaningful latent representations than conventional Next-Token Prediction (NTP).
problem_solved: Overcoming the one-step supervision limitation of NTP, which often produces unstable or unstructured internal world models, by promoting convergence to consistent belief states and semantically aligned latent spaces.
method: Multi-Token Prediction objective: predict blocks of future tokens to shape gradients and enforce multi-step consistency.
Latent Semantic Enhancement: add auxiliary semantic alignment (e.g., contrastive/auxiliary losses or semantic regularizers) to encourage latent states to reflect meaningful factors.
Theory + Empirics: analyze the gradient inductive bias of MTP and validate with experiments showing faster convergence to coherent internal states and improved downstream consistency.
impact: Enables LLMs to form more reliable internal world models, improving multi-step reasoning, planning and state-tracking; useful for building more robust, interpretable, and sample-efficient language agents.
visual_elements: Side-by-side schematic: NTP vs MTP showing one-step vs multi-step supervision and resulting gradient flow
Latent-space illustration: clusters before/after semantic enhancement (colors = semantic factors)
Training curves: convergence speed and consistency metrics comparing NTP, MTP, and MTP+latent enhancement
Qualitative examples: multi-step generation trajectories showing reduced contradictions and improved coherence
paper_title: Toward Consistent World Models with Multi-Token Prediction and Latent Semantic Enhancement
paper_authors: Qimin Zhong, Hao Liao, Haiming Qin, Mingyang Zhou, Rui Mao
